title: What happens if you find your original ball on the course?
question: You hit a provisional ball, but then find your original ball on the course (not out of bounds) within 3 minutes. What should you do next?

choices.text: Pick up the provisional ball and play the original ball
Play whichever ball is in a better position
Play both balls and choose the best result

explanation: You must stop playing the provisional ball and continue with your original ball. Any strokes played with the provisional ball do not count.

juniorVersion.title: What do you do if you find your first ball?
juniorVersion.question: You hit a second ball just in case, but then you find your first ball on the grass before 3 minutes are up. What should you do now?

choices.text: Keep playing the second ball you hit
Pick up the second ball and play your first ball
Choose to play whichever ball is in a nicer spot
Play both balls and choose the better score

juniorVersion.explanation: If you find your first ball, you have to use it. Pick up the second ball you played. Shots with the second ball do not count.

vocabulary.simpleMeaning: A ball you hit just in case you cannot find your first ball.

juniorVersion.teachingTip: Explain that a provisional ball is only used if the first ball cannot be found or goes out of bounds. If the first ball is found in time, the player must use it.
likelyMisconceptions: Kids might think they can always choose the better ball.
Some might not know they must stop playing the provisional ball if the first one is found.
